Define X and Y variables¶

In [38]:
X = df[["Amount", "Gas_Fee_USD", "Daily_Revenue_USD"]]

y = df["Sales_Category"]
In [39]:
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X,
    y,
    test_size=0.20,
    random_state=42
)

Type 1 Error¶

A Type I Error is also called a False Positive (FP). It occurs when the model predicts a positive class (1), but the actual class is negative (0).

Formula:

Type I Error=False Positive (FP) ​

In our model:

From the confusion matrix,

Type I Error=51 ​

Interpretation:

The Logistic Regression model incorrectly classified 51 Low Sales customers as High Sales.

Type 2 Error¶

Type II Error (False Negative)

Definition:

A Type II Error is also called a False Negative (FN). It occurs when the model predicts a negative class (0), but the actual class is positive (1).

Formula:

Type II Error=False Negative (FN) ​

In our model:

From the confusion matrix,

Type II Error=16 ​

Interpretation:

The Logistic Regression model incorrectly classified 16 High Sales customers as Low Sales.

Interpretation¶

The dataset was successfully loaded, explored, and cleaned by handling missing values and removing duplicates to ensure data reliability. A target variable, High_Sales, was then established by using the median sales value to classify transactions as high or low sales.A Logistic Regression model is being developed to predict this binary high-sales outcome using the processed transaction features. The dataset is prepared for training and evaluation to assess the model's classification performance. Overall, this workflow establishes a structured data preprocessing and classification pipeline, transforming raw blockchain and financial data into actionable business insights
